---
title: "DORO: a flat count target the Gamma cannot reach"
subtitle: "Catalog M-09"
description: "Dorazio's KL projection onto a uniform number of clusters: the closest Gamma is a spike plus a hump, the gap grows with n, and the prior ends up expecting about n / 2 clusters."
toc: false
---

Dorazio (2009) asked for the least informative prior on the number of clusters and answered
with a flat one: every K_n from 1 to n equally likely. No Gamma(a, b) hyperprior on alpha can
deliver that, so DORO takes the Gamma whose implied count distribution is closest to flat in
Kullback–Leibler divergence. The explorer solves that problem live for each n.

```{=html}
<div id="w-doro" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/doro-explorer.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxDoro = DPX["doro-explorer"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-doro"), {});
</script>
```

What to look for:

- **The target is out of reach.** With two parameters the closest a Gamma hyperprior gets to
  a flat line is a spike at a single cluster (its shape a < 1 puts mass near alpha = 0) plus a
  hump near 0.9 n (the mass at large alpha), sagging below the target in between. At n = 10
  the solution is Gamma(0.525, 0.046) with KL = .019, Dorazio's own table entry; at n = 50 it
  is Gamma(0.467, 0.0068) with KL = .0705.
- **The gap grows with n and b goes to 0.** The KL divergence rises from .005 at n = 5 to
  .095 at n = 100 while the rate b falls toward 0, so E(alpha) = a / b grows. For Dorazio's
  fish data (n = 53) the solution is Gamma(0.465, 0.0063): E(alpha) = 73 and E K_53 = 28.4.
- **"Noninformative" is a strong statement.** The prior now expects about n / 2 clusters
  among n units (E K_n near n / 2) and no dominant cluster (Pr(W_SB > .5) = .11 at n = 53),
  while every fixed Gamma prior grows like log n.
- **DORO-Unif** (the paper's variant) aims at a flat target on 1 to 2 mu_K − 1 instead. At
  J = 100 and mu_K = 5 the best Gamma is Gamma(2.43, 2.46), a single right-skewed hump: it
  still puts .070 on a single cluster, leaks .073 beyond 9, and gives Pr(W_SB > .5) = .547.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Prior statements only; K_n is the number of fitted components among the n units. Every
(a, b) is solved in the browser by `doroKL` (Nelder–Mead on log a and log b, the same
problem `r-export/05_golden_v2_solvers.R` solves in R; parity against
`verification/golden/solvers.csv`). The two curves under the chart are solved at
n = 5, 10, …, 100 after the page loads.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/doro-explorer.html](../../embed/doro-explorer.html)
(for example `?n=53`, or `?preset=unif10` for DORO-Unif with mu_K = 10).
